=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/review_security_hold_sweep.py:109-123 (_has_current_head_result) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: _has_current_head_result returns True when any current-head result (pending, clean, findings, or failed) exists in the latest 100 comments, which can suppress the full-history REST fallback when the only current-head marker in the window is non-findings and the stale findings marker sits beyond 100 comments.
  WHY: In the specific scenario where a pending marker is within the latest 100 comments and a stale findings marker is beyond them, stale_candidate returns None (latest is pending, not findings), _has_current_head_result returns True (there is a current-head pending), the REST fallback is skipped, and the stale findings never trigger a re-dispatch. This is narrow: a pending within 100 means an in-flight audit already dispatched for that head, so the findings has been addressed. A concrete missed-dispatch requires the pending audit to have silently failed (no result comment posted) AND a findings marker to sit beyond the 100-comment window, which requires both the audit to be broken and the findings to have aged off — a compound edge case with no observed occurrence.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

- scripts/review_security_hold_sweep.py:200-208 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The full comment history is fetched on every scheduled sweep for a PR whose current-head findings marker has aged out of the latest 100 comments, even after the sweep has already dispatched and posted its dedup marker.
  WHY: _has_current_head_result only recognizes security-pass result markers, not the recent sweep marker. The sweep therefore paginates all comments again each tick, then discovers the dedup marker only in stale_candidate. A still-held PR with a large comment history repeatedly consumes one REST request per page on the 30-minute source schedule or hourly consumer schedule.
